lede: Both datasets collapse to one shape: a stroke on digits, a shirt on Fashion-MNIST.
title: Vanilla GAN
question: Do the generator and the discriminator stay stable, and do the samples cover more than one mode?
process: The generator maps noise through a multilayer network that ends in tanh, so each sample lies in [−1, 1]. The discriminator maps an image to one probability. The loss is binary cross-entropy.
One discriminator step scores a real batch against a label of 1 and a generated batch against a label of 0:
The generator step reuses that fake batch with a label of 1, so D(G(z)) is pushed toward 1:
The loop takes one discriminator step, then two generator steps. There is no likelihood.

Trained on 400 images per class for 40 epochs, the digit losses stay near 1.40 and 0.68, and the grid is one stroke, with sample standard deviation 0.0134. On Fashion-MNIST the held-out discriminator loss falls to 0.20, the generator loss rises to 3.43, and the scored grid is one shirt.

opening.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
opening.summary: Both final grids are a single shape, and both score files set the collapse flag. The digit losses barely move. On Fashion-MNIST the generator loss climbs.

beats.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
beats.summary: Epoch 40 on Fashion-MNIST: held-out discriminator loss {eval_d}, generator loss {eval_g}, training generator loss {train_g}, logged sample standard deviation {sample_std}. The discriminator loss fell and the generator loss climbed. The scored batch has sample standard deviation 0.0413, against 0.531 on real images, the collapse flag is set, and every cell is the same shirt. The spread in the training log stayed large, so that series on its own misses the collapse.

reflection.worked: Both runs wrote 40 epochs of loss and a grid at every epoch. The collapse flag matches the pictures: one stroke on digits, and one shirt on Fashion-MNIST.
reflection.unexpected: Digit held-out losses stay near 1.40 and 0.68 while the sample standard deviation ends at 0.012, matching the score file’s 0.0134. On Fashion-MNIST the held-out discriminator loss falls to 0.20 and the generator loss rises to 3.43, but the logged standard deviation ends at 0.641 while the scored batch is 0.041.
reflection.why: The training slice is 400 images per class, and the two standard deviations are the same statistic on different noise draws. On Fashion-MNIST those draws disagree. A reasonable reading is that vanilla binary cross-entropy gives the generator no class to cover, so one image that still fools the discriminator wins.
reflection.improve: Read the grid and the scored sample standard deviation beside the loss. The class-conditional run is the control that stops this collapse. On Fashion-MNIST, where the generator loss runs away, take a smaller discriminator step.
